title: The Legacy of the Galata Colony

mystery.question: What is the story behind the building that now serves as the Jewish Museum of Turkey?
mystery.answer: The building was a synagogue until 1985 and was repurposed in 2001 as a Jewish museum.

briefing: Old Galata has many secrets, and one of them is a building that changed its face over time. Walk from the stone tower to find out what happened to it.

places.clue: Walk to the base of the great stone tower overlooking the Bosphorus.
places.look: Two things here tell a story: one is the writing on the stone, one is the way the tower is built. Photograph the one you trust.

reveal.text: Galata Tower, one of the major landmarks of modern Istanbul, was built in the mid-14th century when the Genoese had a colony at Galata.

links.reason: The writing tells of the Genoese who built this tower. Another place of faith nearby has a building that was rebuilt by the Fossati brothers. Walk past the tower toward the church.
The stone of this tower reminds us of the Genoese colony. Another place of worship nearby was established by the Italian Jewish community. Head toward the street of the synagogue.

places.clue: Follow the path past the tower to the Catholic church.
places.look: Find a detail on the church that speaks of its reconstruction.
places.hint: The church is a short walk from the tower.

reveal.text: The current building is a nineteenth-century reconstruction of the Fossati brothers.

links.reason: The Fossati brothers worked on many buildings here. Now, follow the lanes toward the museum that was once a synagogue.

places.clue: Walk from the tower toward the Italian Synagogue on the street of the synagogue.
places.look: Find a detail on the synagogue that speaks of its Gothic Revival style.
places.hint: The Italian Synagogue is just a short walk from the tower.

reveal.text: In 1931 the original building was demolished and a new Gothic Revival synagogue was built in its place.

links.reason: This synagogue was built by the Italian Jewish community. Another Jewish site nearby was repurposed as a museum. Walk toward the museum.

places.clue: Follow the lanes to the Jewish Museum of Turkey.
places.look: Look at the building's facade and think of its old purpose.
places.hint: The museum is located on Büyük Hendek Street.

reveal.text: The Zülfaris Synagogue, also known as the Kal Kadoş Galata Synagogue, is a former Jewish congregation and synagogue located at 39 Büyük Hendek Street.

finale.text: The building that now serves as the Jewish Museum of Turkey was once the Zülfaris Synagogue, also known as the Kal Kadoş Galata Synagogue. It was used as a synagogue until 1985 and was repurposed in 2001 as a Jewish museum.
